findings.claim: a 8-kilometre sea wall called the Great Wall of Lagos
findings.truth: The Great Wall of Lagos is a planned 8.5 km barrier.

findings.claim: The 2017 opening of the BBC at MediaCityUK
findings.truth: BBC staff began transferring to MediaCityUK in May 2011; ITV Granada followed in 2013.

findings.claim: around 33% of central residents born outside the UK at the 2021 census
findings.truth: The lesson body and its flashcard both say 31.4%; the conclusion contradicted them.

findings.claim: containerised shipping moved to deeper-water ports in the 1970s, the docks closed almost overnight. By 1985 they had lost around 3,000 jobs
findings.truth: Manchester Docks closed in 1982 with the loss of 3,000 jobs; Salford City Council bought the site in 1983.

findings.claim: London charges 15 pounds a day to enter the central zone
findings.truth: The London congestion charge rose to 18 pounds a day on 2 January 2026.

findings.claim: Within two years of expansion, roadside nitrogen-dioxide levels in inner London fell by around 40%
findings.truth: TfL measured NOx in inner London about 20% lower six months after the October 2021 expansion. The 40-54% figures belong to central London.

findings.claim: in Sierra Leone the figure is over 80 (infant mortality per 1,000)
findings.truth: Sierra Leone infant mortality is about 73 per 1,000 live births.

findings.claim: billions live on under US$2.15 a day - the World Bank 2022 extreme poverty line
findings.truth: About 830 million people (10%) live in extreme poverty, and the World Bank line was reset to US$3 a day in 2025.

findings.claim: The average UK citizen lives 26 years longer than a citizen of Sierra Leone; exam tip says Sierra Leone 55
findings.truth: UK life expectancy 81.3, Sierra Leone 57.4 - a gap of about 24 years.
findings.evidence: Wikipedia: List of countries by life expectancy; Demographics of Sierra Leone

findings.claim: A baby born in Norway has roughly 20 times the lifetime income of a baby born in Burundi
findings.truth: The lesson's own GNI figures (Norway US$95,000, Burundi US$240) give a ratio near 400, not 20.

findings.claim: attracting around 600,000 visitors a year before the pandemic
findings.truth: The Gambia recorded about 236,000 international arrivals in 2019.

findings.claim: around 42,000 direct jobs - one in six adults
findings.truth: 42,000 cannot be one in six of about 1.4 million Gambian adults. Over 100,000 Gambians work in tourism directly or indirectly.
findings.evidence: recomputation; Wikipedia: Tourism in the Gambia

findings.claim: one of the world's top ten oil producers
findings.truth: Nigeria ranks about 13th in world oil production at roughly 1.55 million barrels a day.
findings.evidence: Wikipedia: List of countries by oil production

findings.claim: Nigeria is a founder member of ECOWAS, the African Union, OPEC and the Commonwealth
findings.truth: Nigeria founded ECOWAS (1975) and the OAU/AU, but joined OPEC in 1971 and the Commonwealth in 1960, so it founded neither.
findings.evidence: Wikipedia: ECOWAS, OPEC, Commonwealth of Nations

findings.claim: ECOWAS: a regional bloc of 15 countries
findings.truth: ECOWAS has 12 members since Burkina Faso, Mali and Niger formally withdrew on 29 January 2025.

findings.claim: Coastal Lagos is home to Africa's largest stock exchange
findings.truth: The Johannesburg Stock Exchange is far larger. The Nigerian Exchange is the largest and oldest in West Africa.

findings.claim: MCQ 'Which one of the following is a transnational corporation?' offered Dangote Cement as a wrong answer
findings.truth: Dangote Cement operates in about ten African countries, so it is a TNC and the item had two correct answers. Distractors rewritten.
findings.evidence: internal check against the lesson's own text

findings.claim: MTN, providing service to over 200 million Nigerians
findings.truth: MTN Nigeria has about 80 million subscribers; 200 million is the whole sector's line count, not one operator's.

findings.claim: flaring releases CO\u2082 and pollutants (literal escape text stored in the field)
findings.truth: The stored text contains the literal characters CO\u2082, so students see it unrendered in the glossary tooltip and on the flashcard.

findings.claim: the M4 corridor west of London (often called 'Silicon Roundabout's sibling')
findings.truth: 'Silicon Roundabout' is Old Street in London. The M4 corridor's established nickname is the Silicon Corridor.

findings.claim: the Outer Hebrides have seen population fall by over 50% since 1900
findings.truth: The 1901 peak was 46,172 and the 2022 figure 26,140 - a fall of about 43%.

findings.claim: Manchester to Leeds (less than half the distance) can take just as long
findings.truth: Manchester to Leeds by rail is about 43 miles against about 51 miles London to Brighton - shorter, not less than half.

findings.claim: In 1990 coal generated over 70% of UK electricity
findings.truth: Coal supplied about 67% of UK electricity in 1990.
findings.evidence: Wikipedia: Electricity sector in the United Kingdom

findings.claim: 'Examiners reward specific places...', 'markers reward a clear answer...', 'examiners penalise one-sided responses', 'examiners deduct marks for one-sided answers'
findings.truth: No mark scheme deducts or awards marks for these behaviours; a one-sided answer simply cannot reach the top band. All four claims rewritten as plain advice.
findings.evidence: spec assessment section; house rule on fabricated examiner claims

findings.claim: Water scarcity: availability per person per year below 1,700 cubic metres
findings.truth: On the Falkenmark scale below 1,700 cubic metres is water stress; water scarcity is below 1,000.

findings.claim: around 495,000 children under the age of nine
findings.truth: The child diarrhoea death statistic is for children under five; 'under nine' is not a reporting category.

findings.claim: Ethiopia's Grand Renaissance Dam (completed in 2020)
findings.truth: The dam was not complete in 2020; reservoir filling began that year, as the collapsible in the same lesson says.

findings.claim: 140 million people supplied by the South-North Water Transfer Project
findings.truth: The lesson body, key fact, knowledge check and flashcard all say over 185 million; only the conclusion, exam tip and one mark scheme said 140 million.

findings.claim: Groundwater levels rose by an average of around up to 6 metres
findings.truth: 'An average of around up to' is not a meaningful figure; the claim is up to 6 metres.

findings.claim: 24 billion tonnes of topsoil lost per year in one mark scheme
findings.truth: Every other field in the lesson says 25 billion tonnes.

findings.claim: description was 105 characters
findings.truth: The validator limit is under 100 characters.

findings.claim: Lagos is the largest city in Africa
findings.truth: UN agglomeration data put Cairo (about 22 million) above Lagos (about 15-16 million), but AQA-endorsed textbooks and Lagos State's own 20 million+ estimate support the claim. RECOMMENDATION: leave as is; the phrase is standard textbook usage and no examiner would penalise it.
findings.evidence: UN World Urbanization Prospects vs Lagos State estimates
findings.ruling: Leave: textbook figure or unsourced replacement.

findings.claim: large parts of sub-Saharan Africa, South Asia and Central America experience food deficit, with averages below 2,000 kcal
findings.truth: Only a handful of countries (CAR, DRC, Madagascar, Haiti) average below 2,000 kcal; South Asia is about 2,500 and Central America about 2,400. RECOMMENDATION: soften to 'below 2,500 kcal, with the poorest countries under 2,000' once an FAO band is sourced.
findings.ruling: Leave: textbook figure or unsourced replacement.

findings.claim: Around 60 mountainous farming villages had no grid electricity, and the scheme gives power for around 60 households
findings.truth: The same number 60 is used for villages and for households, so one is a slip. RECOMMENDATION: drop the '60 villages' figure and keep '60 households', which matches the Practical Action case study.
findings.ruling: Leave: textbook figure or unsourced replacement.

findings.claim: 'examiners want NAMED schemes' / 'examiners want SPECIFIC Nigerian detail'
findings.truth: Softer than the four claims fixed under F24: these restate the question's own requirement rather than invent a marking behaviour. RECOMMENDATION: leave, or reword to 'the question needs a named scheme' in a later style sweep.
findings.ruling: Leave: textbook figure or unsourced replacement.

findings.claim: Lagos has fewer than 10 metres of road per resident
findings.truth: Literally true but uninformative: the real figure is well under 1 metre per resident.

findings.claim: Open unemployment is officially around 10-15%
findings.truth: Depends entirely on Nigerian NBS methodology: Lagos was 14.6% (2018), 37.1% (2020 old method) and about 5% (2023 new method).

findings.claim: The UK population is just over 67 million; Greater London alone holds over 9 million
findings.truth: ONS mid-2023 gives 68.3 million for the UK and 8.95 million for London.

findings.claim: BedZED in south-east London
findings.truth: BedZED is at Hackbridge in the London Borough of Sutton, south London.

findings.claim: Bristol's closed-loop scheme turns food waste from city schools into compost used on city allotments
findings.truth: Named scheme could not be verified within the WebFetch budget.

findings.claim: in Brazil, the richest 10% earn 38% of national income
findings.truth: World Bank survey data give about 41%; the World Inequality Database gives about 58%.

findings.claim: In 2022 the UN estimated that 281 million people lived outside their country of birth
findings.truth: 281 million is the 2020 migrant stock reported in the 2022 World Migration Report; the 2024 estimate is higher.

findings.claim: Telecoms TNCs like MTN have brought mobile phones to over 200 million Nigerians
findings.truth: Nigeria's active mobile lines fell below 200 million in 2024 after SIM-NIN disconnections, and unique subscribers are far fewer than lines.

findings.claim: produces electric Leaf and Qashqai vehicles
findings.truth: The Leaf is battery-electric; the Qashqai is petrol or e-POWER hybrid, not electric.

findings.claim: Interim targets include reaching net-zero electricity by around 2035
findings.truth: The current UK target is clean power by 2030.

findings.claim: a population of over 220 million (Pakistan)
findings.truth: The 2023 census gives 241 million.

findings.claim: the UN projects that by 2025 two thirds of the world's population could face water shortages
findings.truth: A genuine UN projection, but stated about a year that has now passed.

findings.claim: The UN has identified over 150 potential future water conflict zones globally
findings.truth: Could not be verified; the commonly cited UNEP figure is 300.

findings.claim: an earthquake in Haiti damaged water infrastructure, triggering a cholera outbreak
findings.truth: The death toll (nearly 10,000) is right, but the outbreak was traced to sewage from a UN peacekeeping camp, not to earthquake damage.

findings.claim: Around 21,000 desalination plants operate globally
findings.truth: About 21,000 have been built; roughly 16,000 are operational. The 95 million cubic metres a day figure is correct.

findings.claim: Geographers identify seven main strategies, then eight are listed
findings.truth: The spec lists eight: investment, industrial development, tourism, aid, intermediate technology, fairtrade, debt relief and microfinance loans.

findings.claim: Chinatown on Faulkner Street is one of Britain's oldest
findings.truth: Liverpool has the oldest Chinese community in Europe; Manchester's Chinatown grew from the 1970s and is usually described as the second largest in the UK.

summary: 24 lessons checked against AQA GCSE Geography 8035 sections 3.2.1 to 3.2.3 and the assessment section. 31 FIX findings (2 HIGH), 4 ADJUDICATE and 17 NOTE, delivered as 60 edits. No lesson misstates the paper structure, mark values or SPaG placement; every fault is a case-study figure, a definition, an internal contradiction, a faulty answer key or a fabricated claim about examiner behaviour.
